questions.q: In the PMBOK definition, a project is best described as which of the following?
o: A large collection of unrelated undertakings managed together
A temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result
A permanent organizational function performed by dedicated staff
An ongoing, repetitive effort that sustains a business
questions.e: The PMBOK definition states a project is a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result. The temporary and unique aspects distinguish it from ongoing operations, which are repetitive and sustain the business.

questions.q: How is a 'task' defined in relation to the work breakdown structure?
o: A collection of related projects achieving an organizational goal
Work not included in the work breakdown structure and the lowest level of effort on a project
An element of work with an expected duration, cost, and resource requirement
A group of activities that produces a significant deliverable work product
questions.e: A task is a generic term for work that is not included in the work breakdown structure but could be a further decomposition of work, and it is the lowest level of effort on a project. The choice describing expected duration, cost, and resources defines an activity instead.

questions.q: An element of work performed during a project that normally has an expected duration, cost, and resource requirement, and can be subdivided into tasks, is called a:
questions.e: An activity is an element of work performed during the course of a project, normally having an expected duration, cost, and resource requirement, and activities can be subdivided into tasks.

questions.q: What is the distinction between a program and a portfolio?
o: A program is related projects to achieve an organizational goal, while a portfolio is unrelated projects
A program is a single project, while a portfolio is a phase within it
A program is unrelated projects, while a portfolio is related projects
A program sustains the business, while a portfolio terminates when objectives are met
questions.e: A program is defined as related projects to achieve an organizational goal (e.g., Website, CMS), whereas a portfolio is a set of unrelated projects (e.g., ABC Consulting: BU, CCPA, 1122).

questions.q: A group of activities or tasks that produces a significant deliverable work product is defined as a:
questions.e: A phase is a group of activities/tasks producing a significant deliverable work product. This sits above individual activities and tasks in the hierarchy of work.

questions.q: Which set of elements is common to all definitions of a project?
o: Objective, start and end points, uniqueness, and constraints
questions.e: All project definitions share objective, start and end points, uniqueness, and constraints. People/process/product/technology are the project dimensions, and the initiating/planning/executing/closing set describes project management processes.

questions.q: The characteristic 'progressive elaboration' of a project refers to which idea?
o: Developing in steps and continuing by increments
Having a primary sponsor and customer
questions.e: Progressive elaboration means developing in steps and continuing by increments. Requiring resources, having a sponsor, and involving uncertainty are listed separately as other project attributes.

questions.q: Which characteristics are shared by both projects and operations?
o: Being performed by people, constrained by limited resources, and planned, executed, and controlled
Adopting a new set of objectives so that the work continues
Being temporary, unique, and terminating when objectives are met
Being ongoing, repetitive, and sustaining the business
questions.e: Projects and operations share being performed by people, constrained by limited resources, and being planned, executed, and controlled. Being temporary and unique is specific to projects, while being ongoing and repetitive is specific to operations.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a strategic consideration that projects are implemented to address?
questions.e: The strategic considerations behind projects are a market demand, an organizational need, a customer request, a technological advance, and a legal requirement. A competitor's bankruptcy is not among them.

questions.q: Project management is defined as the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities in order to:
o: Eliminate all uncertainty from the endeavor
Divide unrelated projects into a portfolio
questions.e: Project management is the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet the project requirements, accomplished through processes such as initiating, planning, executing, controlling, and closing.

questions.q: Which sequence lists the project management processes correctly?
o: Initiating, planning, executing, controlling, and closing
questions.e: Project management is accomplished through the processes of initiating, planning, executing, controlling, and closing. The requirements/design/build sequence names project phases, not the management process groups.

questions.q: Managing a project includes balancing the competing demands among which four factors?
questions.e: Managing a project includes balancing the competing demands for quality, scope, time, and cost. People/process/product/technology are instead the four project dimensions.

questions.q: Which of the following is identified as a project management skill?
questions.e: The project management skills are leadership, communications, problem solving, negotiating, influencing the organization, mentoring, and process and technical expertise. Fast tracking is a schedule compression technique, and progressive elaboration is a project characteristic.

questions.q: What are the four project dimensions?
questions.e: The four project dimensions are people, process, product, and technology. Scope/time/cost/quality are the competing demands balanced during management.

questions.q: The practice of overlapping phases that are normally done in sequence is an example of which schedule compression technique?
questions.e: Overlapping phases normally done in sequence is an example of the schedule compression technique called fast tracking. Kill points are another name for phase-end reviews, not a compression technique.

questions.q: According to the common characteristics of project lifecycles, how do cost and staffing levels typically behave over a project?
o: They are low throughout and spike only at the final phase
They are highest at the start and decline steadily to the end
They are low at the start, peak during intermediate phases, and drop rapidly toward conclusion
They remain constant throughout all phases
questions.e: Cost and staffing levels are low at the start, peak during the intermediate phases, and drop rapidly as the project draws to a conclusion. It is stakeholder influence and the risk of failure that are highest at the start.

questions.q: In a typical project lifecycle, when are uncertainty and the risk of failing to achieve objectives greatest?
o: Near the conclusion of the project
At the start of the project
questions.e: The level of uncertainty is highest and the risk of failing to achieve objectives is greatest at the start of the project, with the certainty of completion getting progressively better as the project continues.

questions.q: How does the ability of stakeholders to influence the final characteristics of the product change over the course of a project?
o: It is lowest at the start and gets progressively higher
It peaks during the intermediate phases
It is highest at the start and gets progressively lower
It remains constant across all phases
questions.e: The ability of stakeholders to influence the final characteristics of the product and the final cost is highest at the start and gets progressively lower, while the cost of changes and correcting errors generally increases as the project continues.

questions.q: A measurable, verifiable work product whose completion and approval characterizes a project phase is called a:
questions.e: A deliverable is a measurable, verifiable work product, and the completion and approval of one or more deliverables characterizes a project phase. Phases typically take their names from these deliverables, such as requirements, design, and build.

questions.q: Phase-end reviews are also known by which alternative names?
o: Phase exits, phase gates, or kill points
questions.e: Phase-end reviews are also called phase exits, phase gates, or kill points. These are held to obtain authorization to close the current phase and to initiate the subsequent one.

questions.q: Which of the following best captures the NASA-derived description of a program?
o: A single time-bound undertaking to create one unique result
Work not included in the work breakdown structure
An organized element acting as a whole
A relative series of undertakings continuing over a period of years to accomplish a broad technical or scientific goal
questions.e: Borrowing from NASA, a program is described as a relative series of undertakings that continue over a period of time (normally years) designed to accomplish a broad technical or scientific goal, and it is characterized as large, lengthy, and general. An organized element acting as a whole defines a system.

questions.q: Which three adjectives are used to summarize the nature of a program relative to a project?
questions.e: A program is summarized as large, lengthy, and general, differing from a project mostly in scale and being longer than projects. Temporary, unique, and constrained describe a project instead.

questions.q: Which of the following is defined as 'an organized element acting as a whole'?
questions.e: A system is defined as an organized element acting as a whole. A portfolio is a set of unrelated projects, and a phase is a group of activities or tasks producing a significant deliverable.

questions.q: In the seven core project phases sequence beginning with concept exploration and system exploration, which phase immediately follows Implementation?
questions.e: The phase sequence runs concept exploration, system exploration, requirements, design, implementation, installation, operations and support, maintenance, and retirement. Installation immediately follows implementation.

questions.q: The 40-20-40 rule for allocating software project effort assigns roughly 40% to the first block, 20% to the middle, and 40% to the last. Which three activity groups do these percentages correspond to?
questions.e: The 40-20-40 rule frames effort as roughly 40% Specification, 20% Implementation, and 40% Test, emphasizing that specification and testing together dominate over the coding itself.

questions.q: In a phase-based time allocation comparing project types, a Defense Systems project is characterized by what split of Planning, Code & Unit Test, and Integration & Test effort?
questions.e: Defense Systems allocate 40% to Planning, 20% to Code & Unit Test, and 40% to Integration & Test, mirroring the 40-20-40 rule; Commercial DP by contrast uses 25/40/35.

questions.q: In a comparison of time allocation between a small project (2.5K LOC) and a large project (500K LOC), how does the share of effort spent on Analysis change as the project grows?
questions.e: Analysis grows from 10% on a small (2.5K LOC) project to 30% on a large (500K LOC) project, whereas Code drops from 25% to 10% as size increases.

questions.q: Comparing a small project (2.5K LOC) with a large project (500K LOC), which activity's share of total effort decreases the most as size grows?
questions.e: Code drops from 25% to 10% (a 15-point fall) between small and large projects; Design stays flat at 20%, while Integration and System test actually increase.

questions.q: Which project lifecycle phase is described as the 'Why' phase and is not a mandatory formal phase, sometimes called the 'pre-project' phase?
questions.e: Concept Exploration is the 'Why' phase, an optional pre-project stage covering project idea collection, funneling, and justification via ROI, cost-benefit analysis, and a Project Portfolio Matrix.

questions.q: During Concept Exploration, who is identified as the primary contact for approval and decision making?
questions.e: The project sponsor is identified during Concept Exploration as the primary contact for approval and decision making; the PM, by contrast, coordinates the work rather than granting approvals.

questions.q: The Requirements phase is characterized as the 'What' phase. Which task is called the most difficult in this phase?
o: Writing the Software Project Management Plan
questions.e: Requirements Approval & Sign-Off is described as the most difficult task in the Requirements phase, whose outputs also include the Requirements Document, the first project baseline, and the SPMP.

questions.q: Requirements are divided into two types. Usability, reliability, performance, and supportability are all examples of which type?
questions.e: Non-functional (also called technical) requirements cover everything beyond features, including usability, reliability, performance, and supportability; functional requirements describe features and capabilities.

questions.q: The Analysis & Design phases are collectively described as the 'How' phases. Which document is an output of these phases?
questions.e: Analysis & Design (the 'How' phases) take the Requirements Document as input and produce outputs such as the Functional Specification, Detailed Design Document, User Interface Specification, and Data Model.

questions.q: The Development phase, called the 'Do It' phase, consists mainly of which activities?
questions.e: Development is the 'Do It' phase, covering coding and unit testing, and it often overlaps the Design and Integration phases to shorten the overall schedule.

questions.q: Regarding whether phases appear in the project plan, which statement is accurate?
o: Deployment is typically in the project plan, but maintenance is not
Maintenance is typically in the project plan, but deployment is not
Both deployment and maintenance are typically in the project plan
Neither deployment nor maintenance appears in the project plan
questions.e: Deployment is typically included in the project plan, whereas maintenance is typically not; maintenance covers fixing defects, adding features, and improving performance under strict configuration control.

questions.q: The lifecycle model described as the 'granddaddy' of models features a linear sequence of phases with no overlap in its pure form. Which model is this?
questions.e: Pure Waterfall is called the 'granddaddy' of models: a linear, document-driven sequence of non-overlapping phases with all planning done up-front.

questions.q: Which lifecycle model, nicknamed 'Code-like-Hell,' offers no overhead and requires little expertise but has no process or quality control and is highly risky?
questions.e: Code-and-Fix ('Code-like-Hell') consists of maybe a specification, definitely code, and maybe a release; its advantages are no overhead and little required expertise, but it is highly risky and suited only to prototypes or throwaways.

questions.q: Which lifecycle approach is well suited to rapidly changing requirements, a non-committal customer, and a vague problem domain, though its completion date may be unknown?
questions.e: Evolutionary Prototyping designs the most prominent parts first (often via a visual prototype) and suits rapidly changing requirements and vague domains, but time estimation is difficult and the completion date may be unknown.

questions.q: Which delivery model steps through architectural design in waterfall fashion, then does detailed design, code, test, and delivers in stages, giving customers the product much sooner?
questions.e: Staged Delivery follows waterfall through architectural design, then delivers in stages so customers get the product sooner; its downsides are more required planning and more releases that increase effort and possible feature creep.

questions.q: RAD, popular in the 1980s, proceeds through four steps. What is the correct order of those steps?
o: Joint Application Design, Joint Requirements Planning, Cutover, Construction
Joint Requirements Planning, Joint Application Design, Construction, Cutover
questions.e: Rapid Application Development runs Joint Requirements Planning (JRP), then Joint Application Design (JAD), then Construction (time-boxed, heavy tool use), then Cutover; it suits systems with extensive user input available.

questions.q: COTS refers to a build-vs.-buy decision. What is COTS an acronym for, and what is its main disadvantage?
o: Component Oriented Technical Standard; poor performance
Custom Object Test Suite; higher initial cost
Commercial Off-The-Shelf software; not as tailored to your requirements
questions.e: COTS stands for Commercial Off-The-Shelf software; its advantages are immediate availability and potentially lower cost, while its main disadvantage is being less tailored to your requirements.

questions.q: eXtreme Programming (XP) is described as part of which broader movement, and what is its motto?
questions.e: XP is part of the Agile Development movement, a lightweight, highly incremental/iterative methodology whose motto is 'Embrace Change'; it is notably not a Microsoft product.

questions.q: Lifecycle planning (Lifecycle Management or SDLC) is said to rest on three primary model components. Which set correctly names them?
o: Phases and their order, intermediate products of each phase, and reviews used in each phase
questions.e: The three primary lifecycle model components are the phases and their order, the intermediate products of each phase, and the reviews used in each phase.

questions.q: How many knowledge areas are identified in the project management framework covered here?
questions.e: Nine knowledge areas are identified: Integration, Scope, Time, Cost, Quality, Human Resource, Communications, Risk, and Procurement Management.

questions.q: Which knowledge area is defined as the one that 'defines and controls what is and is not included in the project' and includes creating a Work Breakdown Schedule?
questions.e: Project Scope Management defines and controls what is and is not included in the project; its processes are scope planning, scope definition, creating a Work Breakdown Schedule, scope verification, and scope control.

questions.q: Which knowledge area contains the processes of defining activities, sequencing activities, estimating resource activities, estimating duration, and developing and controlling the project schedule?
questions.e: Project Time Management covers timely completion via defining and sequencing activities, estimating resources and durations, and developing and controlling the schedule.

questions.q: The five project management process groups are Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring & Controlling, and Closing. Which process group is said to usually take the most time and resources?
questions.e: Project Execution usually takes the most time and resources, requiring the PM's leadership skills; a milestone report helps keep focus on completing major milestones.

questions.q: Which process group involves measuring progress toward objectives, monitoring deviation from the plan, and taking corrective action, and is said to affect all other process groups?
questions.e: Monitoring and Controlling measures progress, watches deviation from the plan, and takes corrective action; it affects all other process groups and occurs during all phases of the life cycle.

questions.q: Regarding the mapping of process groups to knowledge areas, which statement is accurate?
o: The Risk Management knowledge area has only Initiating and Closing processes
All initiating activities are part of the Project Integration Management knowledge area
All initiating activities are part of the Project Scope Management knowledge area
Every knowledge area has a process in every process group
questions.e: All initiating activities fall under Project Integration Management, since the Initiating process group has only two processes and both appear in Integration Management; not every knowledge area has a process in every process group.

questions.q: The Risk Management knowledge area is noted as containing processes from only which process groups?
questions.e: The Risk Management knowledge area has only Planning and Monitoring & Controlling processes, illustrating that not every knowledge area spans every process group.

questions.q: How is the fundamental distinction between process groups and knowledge areas characterized?
o: Process groups concern understanding; knowledge areas concern the actions you take
Process groups divide processes by function; knowledge areas divide the same processes by subject matter
Both divide processes by subject matter, differing only in naming
Process groups divide processes by subject matter; knowledge areas divide them by function
questions.e: Process groups divide the processes by function (the actions you take), while knowledge areas divide the same processes by subject matter (the things you need to understand); they are two different views that don't really overlap.

questions.q: A document that formally recognizes the existence of a project, describes the product to be delivered, and addresses the business need is known as the:
questions.e: The project charter is defined as the document that formally recognizes the existence of a project, describing the product to be delivered and addressing the project's business need.

questions.q: In the SMART acronym recommended for a project charter, what does the letter 'A' stand for?
questions.e: A charter should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-specific. The 'A' stands for Achievable.

questions.q: Which pair correctly describes the origin and lifecycle of a project charter?
o: Comes from within the project team and is constantly updated
Comes from outside the project and is constantly updated
Comes from within the project team and remains unchanged during the project
Comes from outside the project and remains unchanged during the project
questions.e: The project charter comes from 'outside' the project, defines the project, and remains unchanged during the project. In contrast, the project management plan is owned by the team and constantly updated.

questions.q: Which document is owned by the project team and constantly updated over the course of the project?
questions.e: The project management plan is owned by the project team and is constantly updated during the course of the project, unlike the charter which stays unchanged.

questions.q: Which of the following is an alternative name used for a project charter?
questions.e: Alternative terms for the project charter include Project Initiation Document, Project Mandate, Project Brief, Letter of Agreement, and Statement of Work. Strategy Plan, Project Execution Plan, and Project Plan are alternative names for the project management plan.

questions.q: The terms 'Strategy Plan', 'Project Execution Plan', and 'Project Plan' are all alternative names for which document?
questions.e: The project management plan is also referred to as Strategy Plan, Project Execution Plan, or Project Plan.

questions.q: What are the two processes involved in project initiation as taken from the PMI handbook?
o: Develop Project Charter and Stakeholder Analysis
Scope Definition and Develop Project Charter
Develop Project Charter and Cost Estimation
questions.e: The two processes in project initiation are Develop Project Charter and Stakeholder Analysis.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as an input to the 'Develop Project Charter' process?
questions.e: Inputs to Develop Project Charter include the project statement of work, business case and/or contract, enterprise environmental factors, and organizational process assets. Constraints and assumptions are outputs of the broader initiating process.

questions.q: Which of the following is an OUTPUT of the initiating process rather than an input?
questions.e: Outputs of the initiating process are the project charter, an assigned project manager, constraints, and assumptions. Product description, strategic plan, project selection criteria, and historical information are inputs.

questions.q: In the project charter template, dates must be entered in which format?
questions.e: The charter template instructs users to enter all dates in the 8-digit MM/DD/YYYY format, such as 02/15/2004.

questions.q: According to the project charter template, a project qualifies as an 'Enterprise Project' when it has significant impact on how many departments?
questions.e: An Enterprise Project is one that has significant impact on 3 or more departments.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed among the 'Reasons for projects'?
questions.e: The reasons for projects are business need, product scope description, and strategic plan.

questions.q: In the distinction between the two documents, which one deals with the 'What' part of the project and defines the vision?
questions.e: The Project Plan is broad, deals with high-level planning and the 'What' part of the project, and defines the vision. The Project Management Plan handles the 'How' part in detail and is executed to achieve the vision.

questions.q: Which statement best characterizes the Project Management Plan when contrasted with the Project Plan?
o: It deals with the 'What' part of the project
It is broad and deals with high-level planning
It is described in very detail and deals with the 'How' part
It defines the vision of the project
questions.e: The Project Management Plan is described in very detail, deals with the 'How' part of the project, and is executed to achieve the vision. Being broad, defining the vision, and covering the 'What' describe the Project Plan.

questions.q: For smaller projects, how are the Project Plan and the Project Management Plan typically handled?
o: They can be merged into one document
They are kept as two entirely separate documents
Only the Project Management Plan is produced
questions.e: For large projects the Project Plan and Project Management Plan are different documents, but for smaller projects they can be merged.

questions.q: The Software Project Management Plan (SPMP) is best described as a document that:
o: Describes how the project would be handled from start to closing and can be seen as an aggregation of other core documents
Revolves solely around the software development plan and describes only what would be developed
Contains only the project budget and schedule
questions.e: The SPMP describes how a project would be handled from start to closing, is considered by some the most important document (along with the SRS), and can be seen as an aggregation of other core documents. Revolving around the development plan and describing what will be developed characterizes the Software Project Plan.

questions.q: Along with which other document is the SPMP considered by some to be the most important document in the project?
questions.e: Some consider the Software Project Management Plan the most important document in the project, along with the SRS (Software Requirements Specification).

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the six components of the Project Management Plan?
questions.e: The Project Management Plan comprises Project Overview, Project Organization, Managerial Processes, Risk Management Process, Technical Process, and Monitoring and Control Mechanisms.

questions.q: The Communications Management Plan, often a section of the SPMP, is chiefly concerned with:
o: Describing information flow to all parties, including gathering and distributing information
questions.e: The Communications Management Plan describes the information flow to all parties, covering the gathering and distributing of information, and addresses status meetings and status reports.

questions.q: Under a project's Control Plans, which of the following is explicitly listed?
questions.e: The Project Plan's Project Control Plans consist of the communication plan, change management plan, risk management plan, and issue management plan.

questions.q: Within the Proposal stage of initiating a project, which of the following is a listed sub-activity?
questions.e: The Proposal stage includes activity analysis, activity attribute analysis, activity scheduling, resource pool analysis and selection, cost estimation, and pricing. Project selection, business development, and award are separate initiation steps.

questions.q: Which item is listed among the common parts of an SDP / SPMP?
questions.e: The common parts of SDP/SPMP are project overview, deliverables, project organization, managerial processes, technical processes, budget, and schedule.

questions.q: In distinguishing planning, estimating, and scheduling activities, what is the specific purpose of the planning step?
o: Assigning specific start and end dates
Determining the size and duration of activities
Identifying the activities to be performed
questions.e: Planning is defined narrowly as identifying the activities. Determining size and duration belongs to estimating, while start/end dates, relationships, and resources belong to scheduling.

questions.q: Estimating, as distinct from planning and scheduling, is concerned with which two attributes of activities?
questions.e: Estimating determines the size of activities and the duration of activities. Specific start/end dates, relationships, and resources are the province of scheduling.

questions.q: Which of the following is a defining component of scheduling but not of planning or estimating?
o: Specifying start and end dates, relationships, and resources
questions.e: Scheduling adds specific start and end dates, relationships between tasks, and resource assignments. Identifying activities is planning, and sizing/duration is estimating.

questions.q: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is best described as which of the following?
o: A hierarchical list of a project's work activities
A Gantt chart of start and end dates
A dependency graph showing task sequencing
questions.e: A WBS is a hierarchical list of the project's work activities. It deliberately does not show dependencies or durations, which distinguishes it from network diagrams and schedules.

questions.q: What are the two formats used to present a Work Breakdown Structure?
questions.e: A WBS can be presented as an indented outline format or as a graphical tree resembling an organizational chart. Gantt charts and network diagrams are scheduling tools, not WBS formats.

questions.q: In the decimal numbering system used for a WBS (for example, 3.1.5), which level is typically assigned the number 0?
o: The top level of the structure
questions.e: In WBS decimal numbering, 0 is typically the top level, with sub-elements numbered by extending the decimal (e.g., 3.1.5). This mirrors the 0.0 top entry seen in the sample outline.

questions.q: Which relationship does a Work Breakdown Structure explicitly show?
questions.e: A WBS shows "is contained in" relationships, indicating how lower elements roll up into higher ones. It does not show dependencies (occurs-before) or durations.

questions.q: Which of the following does a Work Breakdown Structure NOT show?
questions.e: A WBS does not show dependencies or durations; those are captured by network diagrams and schedules. It does include development, management, and project support tasks in a containment hierarchy.

questions.q: Besides development tasks, which additional categories of tasks are included in a WBS?
questions.e: A WBS includes development tasks along with management and project support tasks, giving a complete view of the project's work.

questions.q: A WBS that is activity-oriented (e.g., Requirements, Analysis, Design, Testing) and is typically used by the project manager is which type?
questions.e: A Process WBS is activity-oriented, with elements like Requirements, Analysis, Design, and Testing, and is typically used by the project manager. A Product WBS is entity-oriented instead.

questions.q: A WBS organized around entities such as a financial engine, interface system, and database, typically used by the engineering manager, is which type?
questions.e: A Product WBS is entity-oriented (e.g., financial engine, interface system, database) and is typically used by the engineering manager, whereas a Process WBS is activity-oriented and used by the PM.

questions.q: A hybrid WBS that places lifecycle phases at a high level with component- or feature-specific items within each phase is justified by which rationale?
o: Dependencies must be shown at every level
Products are always more important than processes
questions.e: The Hybrid WBS combines process and product views, with the rationale that processes produce products, so phases can contain component/feature-specific elements.

questions.q: Which WBS development technique involves going only 1-3 levels deep on the first pass, gathering more requirements or data, and adding detail later?
questions.e: The Rolling Wave technique goes 1-3 levels deep initially, then adds more detail after gathering additional requirements or data. Top-Down, Bottom-Up, and Analogy are separate techniques.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the named techniques for developing a WBS?
questions.e: Analogy is listed among WBS development techniques, alongside Top-Down, Bottom-Up, Rolling Wave, and Post-its on a wall.

questions.q: According to the WBS development guidelines, how far should work be broken down?
o: Until accurate time and cost estimates are easy to conceive
Until at least ten levels are reached
Until every task takes exactly one day
questions.e: A guideline states to break work down until accurate time and cost estimates are easy to conceive. There is no fixed level count or one-day rule, and WBS never shows dependencies.

questions.q: One WBS guideline requires that each element of the structure has what?
questions.e: The guidelines state that each WBS element should have an associated deliverable, ensuring the breakdown is outcome-focused.

questions.q: A WBS guideline invokes lessons learned by warning that which of the following often hurts a project most?
questions.e: The lessons-learned guideline notes that what often hurts most is what's missing, motivating careful, complete decomposition of the work.

questions.q: The WBS is described as the basis of many things. Which of the following is one of those things?
questions.e: The WBS serves as the basis for network scheduling, costing, risk analysis, organizational structure, control, and measurement.

questions.q: In the sample retail web site WBS outline, the element 4.0 Site Software Development contains a sub-element 4.2 Backend Software. Which of the following is one of the items listed under 4.2 Backend Software?
questions.e: Under 4.2 Backend Software the outline lists Database Implementation, Middleware Development, Security Subsystems, Catalog Engine, and Transaction Processing. HTML Design/Creation and Content Creation are separate siblings under 4.0, and Requirements Gathering is a top-level 2.0 item.

questions.q: When identifying what needs to be done in order to schedule, dependencies between tasks are captured using which artifacts?
questions.e: Task dependencies are represented with a dependency graph and network diagram as part of identifying what must be done before scheduling. The WBS itself does not capture dependencies.

questions.q: A project is decomposed into which set of elements?
questions.e: A project is described as consisting of functions, activities, and tasks, which underpins the hierarchical decomposition captured in a WBS.

questions.q: The Critical Path Method (CPM) was originally developed in 1957 by which organization and for what purpose?
o: The U.S. Navy for the POLARIS missile program
General Foundry for a product redesign project
The Project Management Institute for software deliverables
E. I. Du Pont de Nemours & Co. for construction of a new chemical plant and maintenance shut-down
questions.e: CPM originated in 1957 with E. I. Du Pont de Nemours & Co. for constructing a new chemical plant and for maintenance shut-down work. The POLARIS/U.S. Navy origin belongs to PERT, not CPM.

questions.q: The Project Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT) was developed in 1958 by the U.S. Navy for which program?
o: The Cables By Us cabling project
questions.e: PERT was created in 1958 by the U.S. Navy for the POLARIS missile program, characterized by non-repetitive R&D work and probabilistic (multiple) task-time estimates.

questions.q: Which set of characteristics correctly describes CPM as opposed to PERT?
o: Three time estimates, beta distribution, milestone-only progress
Multiple task estimates, activity-on-arrow, high time variability
Deterministic task times, activity-on-node construction, repetitive jobs
Probabilistic task times, activity-on-arrow, non-repetitive R&D jobs
questions.e: CPM uses deterministic (single) task times, activity-on-node network construction, and suits repetitive jobs. PERT uses multiple probabilistic estimates, activity-on-arrow construction, and non-repetitive R&D work.

questions.q: In a project network, what does an arrow (leading from tail to head) represent?
o: An activity, a time-consuming effort required to perform part of the work
A dummy relationship requiring no time
An event, a point in time where activities start or finish
questions.e: An arrow indicates an ACTIVITY, a time-consuming effort required to perform part of the work, leading directionally from tail to head. A node (circle) represents an EVENT, a point in time.

questions.q: What is a dummy activity in a network diagram?
o: An activity whose float equals its duration
An activity that indicates only precedence relationships and requires no time or effort
An activity on the critical path with the longest duration
The first activity that starts a project
questions.e: A dummy activity indicates only precedence (sequence) relationships and does not require any time or effort. It is drawn as a dashed line.

questions.q: In an Activity-on-Arrow (AOA) network, what do the nodes represent?
questions.e: In AOA, arrows represent activities while nodes are events (points in time). This contrasts with AON, where nodes represent activities and arrows show precedence relationships.

questions.q: How is the critical path of a project defined?
o: Any path containing a dummy activity
The path with the most activities
The shortest path through the network
The longest path (in time) through the network, which determines the project duration
questions.e: The critical path is the longest path (time) through the network and it determines the overall project duration. Its activities are the critical activities and have zero slack/float.

questions.q: During the forward pass, how is the Earliest Start time (ES) of an activity determined?
o: The maximum Earliest Finish (EF) of its immediate predecessors
The minimum Latest Start of immediate successors
The sum of all predecessor durations
questions.e: In the forward pass, ES equals the maximum EF of the immediate predecessors, and Earliest Finish is EF = ES + t (activity time).

questions.q: An activity has an Earliest Start (ES) of 8 and a duration (t) of 13. What is its Earliest Finish (EF)?
questions.e: Earliest Finish is computed as EF = ES + t. With ES = 8 and t = 13, EF = 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.q: Which formula correctly gives the float (slack) of an activity?
questions.e: Float equals LS - ES, which also equals LF - EF. It is the maximum time an activity can be delayed before it becomes critical and delays project completion; critical activities have zero float.

questions.q: For an activity with Latest Start LS = 2 and Earliest Start ES = 0, what is its slack?
questions.e: Slack = LS - ES = 2 - 0 = 2. Activities on the critical path have zero slack, so a slack of 2 means this activity is not critical.

questions.q: In PERT, the three time estimates required for an activity's duration distribution are:
o: Pessimistic (tp), most likely (tm), and optimistic (to) time
questions.e: PERT assumes an activity's duration follows a probability (beta) distribution and needs three estimates: pessimistic (tp, if things go badly), most likely (tm, the best consensus estimate), and optimistic (to, if things go well).

questions.q: Which formula gives the PERT expected (mean) time te of an activity?
questions.e: The PERT mean/expected time is te = (tp + 4·tm + to)/6, giving four times the weight to the most likely estimate. Equivalently written as (O + 4M + P)/6.

questions.q: Using the beta-distribution formulas, what is the variance var(ti) of an activity whose optimistic time a = 1, most likely m = 2, and pessimistic time b = 9?
questions.e: Variance is var(ti) = (b - a)²/36 = (9 - 1)²/36 = 64/36. (Its expected time would be (1 + 4·2 + 9)/6 = 3.)

questions.q: For the General Foundry PERT example, inspection revealed three paths: A-C-F-H, A-C-E-G-H, and B-D-G-H, with expected durations of 9, 15, and 14 weeks respectively. Which is the critical path?
questions.e: The critical path is the longest, A-C-E-G-H at 15 weeks, since it governs the project's completion time. The other paths (9 and 14 weeks) are shorter and non-critical.

questions.q: For the General Foundry critical path (E(t) = 15 weeks), the total variance was computed as var(t) = 112/36 = 3.11. What is the corresponding standard deviation used in the probability calculation?
questions.e: The standard deviation is the square root of the critical-path variance: √3.11 ≈ 1.76. This 1.76 value is used as σ in the Z-score for project completion probabilities.

questions.q: For General Foundry with expected project time 15 weeks and standard deviation 1.76, the probability of exceeding 16 weeks used a Z value of about 0.57 giving 1 - 0.716. How was that Z value obtained?
Using a standard (less-than) Z-table, P(Z ≤ 1.5) = 0.9332. What is P(Z ≥ 1.5)?
questions.e: Because the Z-table gives only 'less than' probabilities, P(Z ≥ 1.5) = 1 - P(Z < 1.5) = 1 - 0.9332 = 0.0668, since total probability equals 1.00.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts PERT and CPM regarding time estimates and typical use?
o: PERT uses three time estimates and suits R&D projects; CPM uses one time estimate and is used for construction projects
PERT uses one time estimate; CPM uses three
Both use three estimates but only CPM is probabilistic
PERT is deterministic and CPM is probabilistic
questions.e: PERT uses three time estimates, is probabilistic (beta distribution per activity), and suits R&D projects with high time variability. CPM uses one time estimate, is deterministic, and is used for construction projects.

questions.q: For the Cables By Us project the connected paths and durations were: ABDEGHJK = 40, ABDEGIJK = 41, ACFGHJK = 22, ACFGIJK = 23. Which is the critical path?
o: ACFGIJK, because it is the shortest at 23
questions.e: The longest path limits the project duration, so ABDEGIJK (41) is the critical path; the project cannot finish in less time than its longest path.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rule for constructing a CPM network?
o: A project network may have only one start node and only one end node
Time may move in either direction across the network
Nodes have duration while links have none
A network may contain loops but not dangles
questions.e: A CPM network may have only one start node and only one end node. Links (activities) carry duration while nodes do not, time moves left to right, and the network may contain neither loops nor dangles.

questions.q: Which statement about critical paths is correct?
o: A critical path may start at any node and end at any node
A project can have more than one critical path, and the sum of the durations of the activities on a critical path equals the project duration
A project can have at most one critical path
The critical path is the shortest connected sequence of activities
questions.e: A project can have more than one critical path; any critical path starts at node 1 and ends at node n, and the sum of the durations of its activities equals the project's duration.

questions.q: Under PMI's Project Time Management, which process is defined as 'identifying and documenting dependencies among schedule activities'?
questions.e: Activity Sequencing identifies and documents the dependencies among schedule activities. Activity Definition identifies the specific activities, while Schedule Development analyzes sequences, durations, resources, and constraints to build the schedule.

questions.q: In the university website scenario, the management is particular about the home page and expects the company to present at least how many different styles?
questions.e: The scenario states the company is expected to present at least 20 different home-page styles, from which five would be selected.

questions.q: In the university website scenario, once five home-page styles are selected from the presented set, what do those five styles contribute towards?
o: The quality assurance documents for HEC
The style sheets used in CMS development
The layouts possible in the content management system (CMS)
questions.e: The scenario specifies that the five selected styles contribute towards the layouts possible in the content management system (CMS).

questions.q: In the university website scenario, the final requirement is a console through which content can be managed by whom?
questions.e: The scenario's final requirement is a console where content could be managed by the systems and networks administrator of the university.

questions.q: In the university website scenario, each department page requires tabs for several categories. Which of the following is NOT one of the listed department tabs?
questions.e: The department tabs listed are faculty and staff information, courses related information, time tables, and alumni association. Pages for the university's partners are a separate requirement, not a department tab.

questions.q: In the project network, which single activity has the longest duration?
questions.e: Logic development has a duration of 17, the longest of any single activity; Pages development is 15, CMS development 13, and Testing CMS + docs 12.

questions.q: What is the duration assigned to the 'Website design' activity in the project network?
questions.e: Website design has a duration of 6. CMS design is 8, documentation is 5, and content writing is 9.

questions.q: What is the duration of the 'CMS development' activity in the project network?
questions.e: CMS development has a duration of 13, distinct from CMS design (8) and Testing CMS + docs (12).

questions.q: What is the duration of the 'Testing CMS + docs' activity in the project network?
questions.e: Testing CMS + docs has a duration of 12. Testing pages is 9 and Testing logic is 6.

questions.q: Based on the earliest and latest times in the network, what is the total project duration (length of the critical path)?
questions.e: The critical (zero-slack) chain CMS design (8) then CMS development (13) then Testing CMS + docs (12) sums to 33, giving a project duration of 33.

questions.q: In the project network, which sequence of activities forms the critical path (zero slack)?
o: Documentation, Content writing, Testing CMS + docs
Website design, Logic development, Testing logic
CMS design, CMS development, Testing CMS + docs
Website design, Pages development, Testing pages
questions.e: The activities with zero slack (earliest times equal to latest times) are CMS design, CMS development, and Testing CMS + docs, which form the critical path totalling 33.

questions.q: In the project network, the 'Website design' activity has earliest start/finish of 0/6 and latest start/finish of 3/9. What is its slack (float)?
questions.e: Slack equals the difference between latest and earliest start (or finish): 3 minus 0 equals 3, so Website design has 3 units of slack and is not on the critical path.

questions.q: In the work breakdown structure, the 'CMS design' work package is decomposed into which set of components?
o: Style sheets, Administration development, Logic development
Style sheets, Administration prototype, General prototype
Unit testing, Integration testing, System testing
questions.e: CMS design breaks down into style sheets, administration prototype, and general prototype. The development-development-with 'development' components (administration development, logic development) belong to CMS development instead.

questions.q: In the work breakdown structure, the 'CMS development' work package consists of which components?
o: Style sheets, Administration development, Logic development
Style sheets, Administration prototype, General prototype
questions.e: CMS development consists of style sheets, administration development, and logic development, distinguishing it from CMS design which uses prototype components.

questions.q: Within the testing and quality assurance portion of the WBS, test planning is broken into which three levels of testing?
o: Alpha testing, Beta testing, Acceptance testing
Unit testing, Integration testing, System testing
Smoke testing, Regression testing, Load testing
Static testing, Dynamic testing, Manual testing
questions.e: The WBS lists test planning as unit testing, integration testing, and system testing.

questions.q: In the WBS, system testing is annotated with which parenthetical description?
questions.e: The WBS describes system testing as '(sun downing and exit)'.

questions.q: After analysing the schedule, resource issues need to be resolved in order to calculate costs. By what two means is this to be done?
o: Running PERT and generating cash flow reports
questions.e: The stated approach to resolving resource issues (needed to calculate costs) is by rescheduling tasks and adjusting resources.

questions.q: What is the duration of the 'Pages development' activity in the project network?
questions.e: Pages development has a duration of 15, distinct from Logic development (17) and CMS development (13).

questions.q: What is the duration of the 'Content writing' activity in the project network?
questions.e: Content writing has a duration of 9, whereas documentation has a duration of 5.

questions.q: Which schedule compression technique involves taking activities or phases that are normally done in sequence and performing them in parallel for at least a portion of their duration?
questions.e: Fast tracking is defined as a schedule compression technique in which activities or phases normally done in sequence are performed in parallel for at least a portion of their duration. Crashing, by contrast, shortens duration by adding resources rather than by overlapping activities.

questions.q: In the definition of fast tracking, the phrase 'at least a portion of their duration' implies which of the following?
o: Only the first activity in a chain can be overlapped
Entire activities must always be run fully in parallel
Full activities are not required to run in parallel; usually only portions are overlapped
Activities must be fully completed before any overlap begins
questions.e: The wording 'at least a portion of their duration' means full activities are not required to be done in parallel; portions can be overlapped, and most of the time it is only portions that are run in parallel.

questions.q: When schedule compression is required, which technique is explored first?
questions.e: In a situation where schedule compression is required, fast tracking is the technique explored first; crashing is only explored afterward because of its additional cost.

questions.q: Why is crashing always explored only after fast tracking has been considered?
o: Because of the obvious reason of additional cost involved in crashing
Because fast tracking requires more resources
Because crashing cannot be applied to critical path activities
Because crashing is technically harder to plan
questions.e: Crashing is always explored after fast tracking for the obvious reason of the additional cost it introduces, since crashing shortens the schedule by adding resources.

questions.q: Which technique is described as shortening the schedule duration for the least incremental cost by adding resources?
questions.e: Crashing is defined as a technique used to shorten the schedule duration for the least incremental cost by adding resources. Fast tracking instead overlaps sequential activities without necessarily adding resources.

questions.q: In crashing, 'adding resources' can mean which of the following?
o: Approving overtime, paying extra, or adding more resources
questions.e: Additional resources in crashing do not only mean additional heads; they can also include approving overtime, paying extra, or adding more resources.

questions.q: To avoid owning risk without any tangible output, schedule compression techniques should be applied to which activities?
o: Only the first and last activities
The activities with the lowest cost
questions.e: Any schedule compression technique should be applied on critical path activities; otherwise the project may end up owning risk without any tangible output, since only the critical path determines total duration.

questions.q: What is the effect of continuing fast tracking beyond its reasonable limits?
o: It always produces further schedule compression
It may only add risk and rework rather than schedule compression
It automatically converts the activity into crashing
It reduces the project cost significantly
questions.e: Fast tracking can only be done to some limits, after which continuing may only add risk and rework and not schedule compression, illustrated by the idea that you must wait for concrete to settle before starting painting.

questions.q: What happens if crashing is continued beyond its useful limit?
o: It keeps compressing the schedule indefinitely
It removes activities from the critical path
It may only consume money without achieving schedule compression
It converts fixed costs into variable costs
questions.e: Crashing can only be done to some limits, after which continuing may only consume money without producing schedule compression, illustrated by the idea that you cannot deliver a baby in one month even if resources increase from 1 to 9.

questions.q: Which formula is used to calculate the crash cost slope of an activity?
o: (Crash time - normal time) / (crash cost - normal cost)
(Normal cost + crash cost) / (normal time + crash time)
(Crash cost - normal cost) / (crash time - normal time)
(Normal cost - crash cost) / (normal time - crash time) squared
questions.e: The slope, representing crash cost per unit of time saved, is calculated as (crash cost - normal cost) divided by (crash time - normal time).

questions.q: An activity has a normal time of 4 weeks, a crash time of 2 weeks, a normal cost of 13,000, and a crash cost of 25,000. What is its cost per week to crash?
An activity has a normal time of 4 weeks, a crash time of 1 week, a normal cost of 11,000, and a crash cost of 18,000. What is its approximate cost per week to crash?
questions.e: The cost per week is (18,000 - 11,000) / (4 - 1) = 7,000 / 3, which is approximately 2,333 per week.

questions.q: In a crashing example, an activity has equal normal and crash times of 1 week, with both normal and crash cost at 9,000. What does this indicate about the activity?
o: It has the highest crash cost per week
It is the most expensive activity to crash
It cannot be crashed further and has zero crash cost per week
It is off the critical path
questions.e: With a normal time equal to its crash time (1 week) and identical normal and crash costs (9,000), the activity has zero weeks available to decrease and a cost per week of 0, meaning it cannot be crashed.

questions.q: In a network with paths A-B-D-H-I = 22, A-B-E-H-I = 18, A-B-E-G-I = 18, A-C-E-H-I = 17, A-C-E-G-I = 17, and A-C-F-G-I = 19, which is the critical (longest) path?
questions.e: The critical path is the longest path through the network. Here A-B-D-H-I has a duration of 22, which is longer than all other listed paths, making it critical.

questions.q: In the network with paths A-B-D-H-I = 22, A-C-F-G-I = 19, A-B-E-H-I = 18, and A-C-E-H-I = 17, what is the length of path A-C-F-G-I?
questions.e: Path A-C-F-G-I has a stated total duration of 19, making it the second-longest path in the network after the critical path A-B-D-H-I at 22.

questions.q: In a project with activities A (7 days, no predecessor), B and C (both preceded by A), D (preceded by B and C), E and F (preceded by D), and G (preceded by E and F), which activity has no immediate predecessor?
questions.e: Activity A, with a duration of 7 days, has 'None' as its immediate predecessor, making it the starting activity of the network.

questions.q: For a project with paths ABDFG = 24, ABDEG = 22, ACDFG = 25, and ACDEG = 23, which path is critical before any crashing?
questions.e: ACDFG has the longest length at 25, so it is the critical path that initially determines the project duration.

questions.q: In the crashing exercise where the paths ABDFG (24), ABDEG (22), ACDFG (25), and ACDEG (23) are compressed, all four paths are reduced to what common length after crashing the project by 4 days?
questions.e: After crashing the project by 4 days, the sequence of crash actions brings all four paths (ABDFG, ABDEG, ACDFG, ACDEG) down to a length of 21.

questions.q: In the time-cost crashing exercise, crashing actions are taken in the order Crash A ($1,000), Crash C ($1,200), Crash F ($1,500), and Crash F ($1,500). What is the total cost accumulated after all four actions?
questions.e: The marginal costs accumulate as $1,000, then $2,200, then $3,700, then $5,200, giving a total crashing cost of $5,200 after the four actions.

questions.q: In the time-cost crashing table, activity A has a normal time of 7 days, crash time of 6 days, normal cost of $7,000, and crash cost of $8,000. What is its cost per day to crash?
questions.e: The cost per day is (8,000 - 7,000) / (7 - 6) = 1,000 / 1 = $1,000 per day, which is why Crash A is chosen first as the cheapest action.

questions.q: In the time-cost crashing table, activity F has a normal time of 4 days, crash time of 2 days, normal cost of $4,000, and crash cost of $7,000. What is its cost per day to crash?
In the time-cost crashing table, which activity has the highest crash cost per day at $3,000?
questions.e: Activity G (normal 5 days/$5,000, crash 4 days/$8,000) has a cost per day of (8,000 - 5,000) / (5 - 4) = $3,000, the highest per-day crash cost in the table.

questions.q: Which three primary methods are used for determining the projected financial value of projects?
o: Weighted scoring, ROI, and cost-benefit ratio
Net present value, return on investment, and payback analysis
Discounted cash flow, opportunity cost, and liquidity ratio
questions.e: The three primary methods for determining a project's projected financial value are Net Present Value (NPV) analysis, Return on Investment (ROI), and Payback analysis. Margin and turnover are components of ROI, not stand-alone methods, and weighted scoring is a separate multi-criteria selection tool.

questions.q: Price is described as having two components. Which equation expresses this relationship?
questions.e: Price has a component of cost and a component of profit, expressed as P = C + Profit. It is a sum of the two components, not a difference, quotient, or product.

questions.q: How is Net Present Value (NPV) defined?
o: The product of margin and turnover across operating assets
A method of calculating the expected net monetary gain or loss from a project by discounting all expected future cash inflows and outflows to the present point in time
Income divided by the initial investment expressed as a percentage
The amount of time needed to recoup the net dollars invested in a project
questions.e: NPV is a method of calculating the expected net monetary gain or loss from a project by discounting all expected future cash inflows and outflows to the present point in time. Income divided by investment describes ROI, and time to recoup investment describes payback.

questions.q: When financial value is a key criterion, which projects should be considered under NPV analysis?
o: Projects with an NPV of exactly zero
questions.e: Projects with a positive NPV should be considered when financial value is a key criterion, and the higher the NPV the better. Negative or zero NPV projects are not preferred.

questions.q: A Treasury Bill will be worth $400,000 one year from today and Treasury bills carry a risk-free rate of 7%. What is its present value today?
questions.e: The present value is $400,000 / (1.07) = $373,832. The $400,000 is the future value, and $350,000 is the cost of the alternative building project in the same example.

questions.q: Land can be bought for $50,000 and a building constructed on it for $300,000, after which the building can be sold in one year for $400,000 with certainty. At a 7% risk-free discount rate, what is the NPV of this project?
questions.e: NPV = PV - Required Investment = [$400,000/(1+0.07)] - $350,000 = $373,832 - $350,000 = $23,832. The total investment is $50,000 + $300,000 = $350,000, and $7,143 is the NPV in the higher-risk 12% scenario.

questions.q: If the same building project promising $400,000 in one year is treated as risky as a stock yielding 12%, what is its NPV given a $350,000 investment?
questions.e: At a 12% opportunity cost of capital, NPV = [$400,000/(1+0.12)] - $350,000 = $357,143 - $350,000 = $7,142.86, roughly $7,143. This is much less than the $23,832 NPV at the 7% risk-free rate, showing the project is less attractive once risk is accounted for.

questions.q: What is the discount rate used in an NPV calculation called?
questions.e: The discount rate is known as the opportunity cost of capital, because it is the return you give up by investing in the project instead of the alternative. Margin and turnover are ROI components.

questions.q: Which basic financial principle follows from an NPV falling when a project's risk increases?
o: A safe dollar is worth less than a risky one
All dollars have equal present value
A risky dollar is worth less than a safe one
Risk has no effect on present value
questions.e: Because a higher opportunity cost of capital reduces the discounted value of future cash flows, the principle is that a risky dollar is worth less than a safe one. This is why a riskier project is discounted at a higher rate and shows a lower NPV.

questions.q: For a 10-month project billing a client Rs. 1,000,000 total with an expense of Rs. 85,000 per month and an ending balance of Rs. 115,000, what is stated as the profit?
questions.e: The profit is Rs. 115,000, the final balance after all inward transactions and expenses. Rs. 1,000,000 is the total investment/contract value, Rs. 85,000 is the monthly expense, and Rs. 61,095 is the risk-adjusted 'current situation' figure.

questions.q: In the project cash-flow schedule, what percentage of the Rs. 1,000,000 is received as the mobilization advance in the first month?
questions.e: The mobilization advance is 10% (Rs. 100,000) received in month 1. SRS finalization is 15%, the first release is 35%, and the final release is 20%.

questions.q: In the payment schedule, when is the final 20% of the contract value released?
o: At the mobilization stage before work begins
Upon expiry of the maintenance period, usually 6 months to 1 year after final acceptable delivery
questions.e: The remaining 20% is given upon expiry of the maintenance period, usually 6 months to 1 year after final acceptable delivery is made. The other milestones (mobilization, SRS, first release) occur earlier in the project.

questions.q: With a total gain of Rs. 1,115,000 expected and a bank rate of return of 5%, the present value is Rs. 1,061,905. What is the resulting difference (1,115,000 - 1,061,905)?
questions.e: 1,115,000 - 1,061,905 = Rs. 53,095 is the discount amount. Subtracting this from the Rs. 115,000 profit gives the risk-adjusted 'current situation' of Rs. 61,095.

questions.q: How is Return on Investment (ROI) defined in terms of discounted figures?
o: Total discounted benefits / total discounted costs
(Total discounted benefits - total discounted costs) / discounted costs
(Total discounted costs - total discounted benefits) / discounted benefits
questions.e: ROI equals income divided by investment, specifically (total discounted benefits - total discounted costs) / discounted costs. The higher the ROI, the better.

questions.q: ROI can be decomposed into two factors. What is that relationship?
questions.e: ROI = Margin * Turnover, where Margin = Net operating income / Sales and Turnover = Sales / Average operating assets. It is a product of the two, not a sum, quotient, or difference.

questions.q: How is Turnover computed in the ROI breakdown?
o: Net operating income / Average operating assets
questions.e: Turnover = Sales / Average operating assets. Net operating income / Sales is Margin, and Net operating income / Average operating assets is ROI itself.

questions.q: A company reports net operating income of $30,000, sales of $500,000, and average operating assets of $200,000. What is its ROI computed as margin times turnover?
questions.e: Margin = $30,000/$500,000 = 6%, Turnover = $500,000/$200,000 = 2.5, so ROI = 6% * 2.5 = 15%. The 6% is only the margin, and 21.8% is the improved ROI after an equipment investment in a later example.

questions.q: After investing $30,000 in equipment, a company reports net operating income of $50,000, sales of $535,000, and average operating assets of $230,000. What does its ROI become?
questions.e: Margin = $50,000/$535,000 = 9.35%, Turnover = $535,000/$230,000 = 2.33, so ROI = 9.35% * 2.33 = 21.8%, up from the prior 15%. The 9.35% is only the margin and 2.33 is only the turnover.

questions.q: What does the 'payback period' measure?
o: Income divided by investment expressed as a percentage
The total weighted score of a project across weighted criteria
The amount of time it takes to recoup, in net cash inflows, the net dollars invested in a project
The net monetary gain from a project after discounting all cash flows
questions.e: The payback period is the amount of time it will take to recoup, in the form of net cash inflows, the net dollars invested in a project. Net monetary gain from discounting describes NPV, and income over investment describes ROI.

questions.q: A project has cash flows of -$165,000 in Year 0, $63,120 in Year 1, $70,800 in Year 2, and $91,080 in Year 3, giving cumulative balances of -$101,880, -$31,080, and $60,000. What is its payback period?
questions.e: After Year 2 the cumulative cash flow is -$31,080, so payback = 2 + (31,080/91,080) = 2.34 years. It occurs partway through Year 3 because the investment is not fully recovered until then.

questions.q: What is the decision rule for accepting a project under payback analysis?
o: Accept if the payback period is less than some preset limit
Accept only if the payback period equals zero
Accept if the payback period is greater than some preset limit
Accept if the payback period exceeds the project duration
questions.e: The decision rule is to accept the project if the payback period is less than some preset limit, since many organizations want IT projects to have a fairly short payback period.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a DISADVANTAGE of the payback method?
o: It accounts for all cash flows over the project's life
It ignores the time value of money
questions.e: Disadvantages of payback include ignoring the time value of money, requiring an arbitrary cutoff point, and ignoring cash flows beyond the cutoff date. Being easy to understand and biased towards liquidity are its advantages.

questions.q: In a weighted scoring model, what must be true of the weights assigned to each criterion?
o: They are scores that add up to the number of projects
They are percentages that add up to 100%
They are discount rates summing to the opportunity cost of capital
questions.e: In a weighted scoring model, weights (percentages) are assigned to each criterion so they add up to 100%; scores are then assigned per criterion and multiplied by weights to get total weighted scores, and the higher the weighted score the better.

questions.q: In most software projects, which category is identified as the dominant cost factor?
o: Overheads such as heating and lighting
questions.e: Effort costs, comprising the salaries of engineers plus social and insurance costs, are described as the dominant factor in most projects, unlike hardware/software, travel/training, or overhead costs.

questions.q: When accounting for effort costs, overheads must be taken into account. Which technique is grouped under overheads for allocating such costs?
questions.e: Overheads include building/heating/lighting, networking and communications, shared facilities, asset depreciation, and Activity Based Costing (ABC). DSI, Wideband-Delphi and PROBE are size/estimation concepts, not overhead items.

questions.q: One survey of software failure reported that 53% of projects cost roughly what proportion of their original estimate?
questions.e: The figure cited is that 53% of projects cost almost 200% of their original estimate, alongside an estimated $81 billion spent on failed U.S. projects in 1995, all of which used the waterfall lifecycle.

questions.q: A British Computer Society (BCS) survey examined 1027 projects. How many of these were reported as successful?
questions.e: Out of 1027 projects in the BCS survey, only 130 were successful, where success meant delivering all system requirements within budget, within time, and to the quality agreed on.

questions.q: Which relationship is used to express software price in terms of cost?
questions.e: Cost estimation is needed early because software price is defined as cost plus profit; there is no simple relationship between development cost and the price charged, which is also shaped by organisational, economic, political and business factors.

questions.q: Productivity measures are divided into two families. Which measure is named as the best known function-related measure?
questions.e: Function-related measures are based on an estimate of the functionality of delivered software, and function points are named as the best known measure of this type; size-related measures such as lines of code and object code instructions belong to the other family.

questions.q: In the software pricing factors, what behaviour is associated with 'requirements volatility'?
o: Lowering the price to enter a new market segment for future profit
Allowing the developer to retain source code ownership in exchange for a lower price
Lowering the price to win the contract, then charging high prices for later requirement changes
Raising the price by a contingency because the cost estimate is uncertain
questions.e: Under requirements volatility, if requirements are likely to change an organisation may lower its price to win the contract and then charge high prices for changes after the contract is awarded. The other options describe cost estimate uncertainty, market opportunity, and contractual terms respectively.

questions.q: Why is the origin of the 'line of code' measure tied to punched cards?
o: Cards enforced a linear relationship between size and complexity
The measure was first proposed when programs were typed on cards with one line per card
Cards counted declarations but ignored comments
Cards limited programs to exactly one thousand lines
questions.e: The LOC measure was first proposed when programs were typed on cards with one line per card, which is why applying it to modern languages where statements span multiple lines is problematic.

questions.q: Under the Delivered Source Instructions (DSI) counting rules, how are declarations and comments handled?
o: Comments are counted, but declarations are not
Both declarations and comments are counted
Neither declarations nor comments are counted
Declarations are counted, but comments are not counted
questions.e: Under DSI, one instruction is one LOC, declarations are counted, and comments are not counted.

questions.q: What paradoxical conclusion follows from measuring productivity using lines of code?
o: LOC measures show quality and productivity are identical
Higher-level languages make programmers appear less productive
Programmers who write verbose code appear more productive
Programmers who write compact code appear more productive
questions.e: Because the same functionality takes more code in lower-level languages, LOC-based productivity suggests that programmers who write verbose code are more productive than those who write compact code.

questions.q: The function point count is built from a combination of program characteristics. Which set of characteristics is used?
o: Precedentedness, team cohesion, and process maturity
External inputs/outputs, user interactions, external interfaces, and files used
Rule sets, screen definitions, and user reports
questions.e: Function points are based on external inputs and outputs, user interactions, external interfaces, and files used by the system, each with an associated weight. Screens, reports and 3GL modules belong to object points, while precedentedness, team cohesion and process maturity are COCOMO II scale factors.

questions.q: Function points can be converted to lines of code using LOC = AVC x number of function points. What range of AVC values is given for Assembly language?
questions.e: AVC is a language-dependent factor varying from 200-300 for Assembly language down to 2-40 for a 4GL, so verbose low-level languages have a much higher LOC-per-function-point value.

questions.q: What limitation is stated regarding the automation of function-point counting?
o: Automatic function-point counting is impossible because FPs depend on the estimator
Automatic counting requires historical regression data
Automatic counting is trivial and fully objective
Automatic counting only works for 4GL languages
questions.e: Function points are described as very subjective and dependent on the estimator, and automatic function-point counting is stated to be impossible.

questions.q: The function points approach was popularized by the extensive research of which two people?
questions.e: The function points approach was popularized by the extensive research of A.J. Albrecht and J.E. Gaffney, and it is considered better than LOC because it measures software size from the specification early in the life cycle.

questions.q: Which criticism of the function point approach concerns the Technical Complexity Factor (TCF)?
o: TCF was calibrated from 63 software projects
TCF replaces the need for the Unadjusted Function Count
Internal complexity is double counted in the UFC and again in the TCF, and TCF does not improve accuracy over UFC
TCF weights are measured on an absolute scale
questions.e: Internal complexity is counted both when assigning weights in the UFC and again in the TCF (double counting), and researchers have shown that TCF does not improve accuracy over UFC. Weights and TCF ratings are on an ordinal scale while counts are on an absolute/ratio scale.

questions.q: The number of object points in a program is a weighted estimate of which items?
o: Separate screens (forms), reports produced, and 3GL modules needed to supplement 4GL code
Object classes, methods, and inheritance links
External inputs, outputs, and user interactions
questions.e: Object points are a weighted estimate of the number of separate screens (forms) displayed, the number of reports produced, and the number of 3GL modules that must be developed to supplement the 4GL code; they are explicitly not the same as object classes.

questions.q: Who developed the object points measure and for what type of project was it originally intended?
o: Albrecht et al., originally for information systems
Banker et al., originally for CASE tool development projects
Reifer et al., originally for web development projects
Boehm et al., originally for waterfall projects
questions.e: Object points were developed by Banker et al., originally intended for CASE tool development projects, later adapted for object-oriented software, and use object counts instead of function counts.

questions.q: In the object points method, if a program is not entirely new, the New Object-Point (NOP) is calculated as which expression, where RF is the reuse factor?
questions.e: After summing complexity weights to get the Object-Point (OP) and multiplying by a reuse factor, the New Object-Point for a non-new program is NOP = OP (1 - RF), and effort is then NOP divided by the productivity cost.

questions.q: In the object points productivity table indexed by developer experience and ICASE maturity, what is the productivity cost value at the 'Nominal' level, and how is effort computed from it?
o: 25, with Effort = NOP x Productivity cost
questions.e: The productivity cost values run 4 (Very Low), 7 (Low), 13 (Nominal), 25 (High), 50 (Very High), and effort is Effort = NOP / Productivity cost.

questions.q: What does the PROBE size estimation method stand for, and what does it require to function?
o: Proxy Based Estimation, requiring historical data
Project Based Estimation, requiring object classes
questions.e: PROBE stands for PROxy Based Estimation, using proxies such as function points or object points instead of SLOC, and it requires historical data (it does not work without it) for linear regression analysis.

questions.q: Which statement correctly characterises the Wideband-Delphi estimation method with respect to historical data and bias?
o: It requires large amounts of historical data and is more biased than individual estimation
It does not require historical data and is less biased than individual estimation
It requires a regression line and eliminates all consensus errors
It can only be applied at the whole-project level, never at component level
questions.e: Wideband-Delphi is an iterative, team-based, collaborative method that is less biased than individual estimation and does not require historical data; it can be applied at both high-level and detailed levels, though it risks consensus on an incorrect estimate.

questions.q: How do top-down and bottom-up cost estimation differ in their applicability?
o: Top-down is usable without knowledge of the system architecture, while bottom-up requires the architecture known and components identified
Neither can account for integration costs
Top-down needs the architecture known, while bottom-up is usable without it
Both require a fully detailed design before use
questions.e: Top-down estimation is usable without knowledge of the system architecture and can underestimate difficult low-level technical problems, whereas bottom-up estimation is usable when the architecture is known and components are identified, and may underestimate system-level activities like integration.

questions.q: The COCOMO'81 model was derived from the analysis of how many software projects, and in what year?
questions.e: COCOMO'81 is an empirical model derived from the analysis of 63 software projects in 1981, while COCOMO II (2000) accounts for different development approaches and reuse.

questions.q: In the COCOMO II early design model PM = A x Size^B x M + PMm, what is the value of A in the initial calibration and the range of the exponent B?
